theme: Agur’s words; King Lemuel; the excellent wife
readingInstruction: Read Proverbs 30:1-31:31. The book ends with the words of Agur, the words of King Lemuel, and the famous poem of the excellent wife. Read the final poem as the capstone of the book, and ask who she really is.
settingTheScene: Chapter 30 is attributed to Agur, an otherwise unknown man, and includes numerical sayings and a prayer. Chapter 31 begins with what a queen mother taught her son the king, and ends with an acrostic poem in praise of “an excellent wife.” It is the final word of Proverbs. Since the book opened with wisdom as a woman calling in the street, it closes with a portrait of wisdom lived out.
observation: “Surely I am more brutish than any man. I have not the understanding of a man” (30:2).
“Who has ascended to heaven and come down?… What is his name, and what is his son’s name? Surely you know!” (30:4).
“Every word of God proves true; he is a shield to those who take refuge in him” (30:5).
“Give me neither poverty nor riches; feed me with the food that is needful for me” (30:8).
“Open your mouth for the mute, for the rights of all who are destitute” (31:8).
“An excellent wife who can find? She is far more precious than jewels” (31:10).
“Strength and dignity are her clothing, and she laughs at the time to come” (31:25).
“Charm is deceitful, and beauty is vain, but a woman who fears the LORD is to be praised” (31:30).
interpretation:
Agur begins with a confession of humility, almost despairing. He claims no wisdom. He then asks rhetorical questions about who has ascended into heaven and gathered the wind in his fists, “What is his name, and what is his son’s name?” The questions point to the mystery of God. He knows his limits. And then comes a statement of faith: “Every word of God proves true; he is a shield to those who take refuge in him.” The proper response to our limits is not despair but trust in God’s word.

Agur’s prayer in verses 7 to 9 is a model of balanced petition. “Give me neither poverty nor riches.” He fears wealth, lest he deny God, and poverty, lest he steal. It shows self-knowledge. He asks for enough. The numerical sayings that follow, “Three things are too wonderful for me… four I do not understand,” show wonder at creation.

The words of King Lemuel are a mother’s teaching to her son. She warns against indulgence and calls him to speak up for those who have no voice. “Open your mouth for the mute.” A good ruler is an advocate for the helpless.

The final poem, the “excellent wife,” is an acrostic, each line beginning with the next letter of the Hebrew alphabet, a completeness from A to Z. She is a woman of strength, wisdom, industry, generosity, and fear of the LORD. She works with her hands, manages her household, trades, invests, gives to the poor, and teaches with kindness. The poem is not a checklist of tasks a woman must do. It is a portrait of wisdom embodied. The word “excellent” is the same word used elsewhere for a “mighty” warrior. It is a picture of valor.

The key line is verse 30: “Charm is deceitful, and beauty is vain, but a woman who fears the LORD is to be praised.” The book ends where it started: with the fear of the LORD. Wisdom is not an abstraction. It takes shape in a life lived under God.
connection: Agur’s question, “Who has ascended to heaven and come down?” finds its answer in Christ (John 3:13; Ephesians 4:9-10). “Every word of God proves true” is echoed in Jesus’ trust in the Scriptures (Matthew 5:18). Ephesians 5:25-27 shows Christ’s love for the church as a bride. Jesus said, “Give us this day our daily bread” (Matthew 6:11), the prayer of Agur’s “food that is needful.”
application:
Pray Agur’s prayer: ask God for “enough” and not too much or too little.

Whether man or woman, read the Proverbs 31 poem as a portrait of wisdom to imitate.

Speak up for someone who has no voice this week.
prayerPrompts: Thank God that every word of his proves true.
Ask him for neither poverty nor riches but what you need.
Ask him to teach you to open your mouth for those who cannot speak for themselves.
